site.name: Kurisu Labs
site.description: Kurisu Labs is an independent research and engineering collective exploring blockchain, Web3, and decentralized systems across ecosystems.

hero.title: Exploring ideas. Building working systems.
hero.body: We explore blockchain and decentralized systems through research and practical engineering—building experimental products, developer tools, and infrastructure across ecosystems.

directions.title: Questions we’re exploring
directions.intro: Our current focus is blockchain and decentralized systems: how they work, where they help, and what it takes to build with them.

approach.title: Small teams. Open questions. Practical experiments.
approach.body: We work in small, project-led teams. We investigate a question, build a prototype, test its assumptions, and decide what is worth developing further. Some experiments become tools or products. Others become useful findings and new questions.

collaboration.title: Explore a technical question with us.
collaboration.body: We’re interested in collaborations that connect research with real engineering needs—from developer tooling and blockchain prototypes to practical Web2–Web3 integrations.
collaboration.supportingLine: A fully decentralized system is not always the answer. Sometimes the useful result is a simpler design, a hybrid architecture, or a clearer understanding of the trade-offs.

directions.title: Blockchain infrastructure & developer tooling
directions.question: How can we make blockchain systems easier to build, inspect, and maintain?
directions.description: We explore developer tools and infrastructure for building, inspecting, and maintaining applications across blockchain ecosystems.

directions.title: Privacy, identity & verifiable systems
directions.question: What can a system prove without revealing more than it needs to?
directions.description: We investigate approaches to privacy, identity, and verification through experiments with cryptographic and decentralized technologies.

directions.title: AI & decentralized coordination
directions.question: How can intelligent systems interact with shared infrastructure?
directions.description: We explore the interfaces between AI-enabled applications, coordination mechanisms, and decentralized systems.

directions.title: Applied decentralization & Web2–Web3 integration
directions.question: Where does decentralized infrastructure make an existing system meaningfully better?
directions.description: We investigate practical Web2–Web3 integrations, including hybrid approaches to ownership, trust, privacy, and coordination.
